To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the production of fully ES cell-derived mice can be achieved with a high efficiency by using a conventional blastocyst microinjection technique, which can be performed by any laboratory without the use of laser or piezo systems.
the production of F0 ES-derived mice can be achieved using the conventional blastocysts injection method without the use of laser or piezo micromanipulation instruments.
the activation of embryonic stem cells and appropriate culture conditions for both the stem cells and the embryos are crucial for the production of F0 embryonic-stem-cell-derived mice.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of new technologies to produce transgenic animals and to study the molecular mechanisms of mammalian development.

improving the conventional method of producing F0 ES cell-derived mice by optimizing the culture media for both ES cell and embryos and by injecting ES cells into the eight-cell embryo instead of the blastocyst.
the development and optimization of a simple and inexpensive technique to produce F0 mice from ES cell lines.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the production of F0 ES mouse pups is a complex and time-consuming procedure, and it requires careful optimization of all the steps involved.

the use of ES cells that are activated before injection, in combination with blastocysts that are cultured in a medium optimized for ES cells, and the injection of blastocysts in oviducts of 0.50.5-day pseudopregnant CD1 females, increases the production of F0 ES mouse pups with full germlinetransmission.
the production of F0 mice is a complex process that depends on many factors.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have developed an economical, efficient and simple method for producing F0 ES cell-derived mice with full germlinetransmission, which can be easily applied in many laboratories.

1) activating the ES cells before injection is essential to increase the efficiency of chimeric and ES cell-derived F1 offspring, 2) culture media optimized for the survival and development of embryos are crucial to increase the number of chimeric animals, 3) the site of embryo transfer is important to increase the proportion of chimeras and the number of ES cell-derived F 0 offspring.

the activation of the injected cells and the appropriate conditions for in vitro culture of the manipulated embryos are critical for the production of F0 ES mouse pups, whereas the site of embryo transfer is important to increase the proportion of chimeras and the efficiency of production.
The main takeaway from our work is that

activation of ES cells before blastocyst injection, the use of culture conditions that support the survival of both embryos and ES cells, and transferring embryos to the oviduct increase the production of F0 ES pups.

the use of the appropriate culture conditions and the transfer of the injected embryos into the ooviduct of 0,5 day pseudopregnant mice is crucial for the production of F0 ES cells mice with full germlin transmission.
activation of ES cells is crucial for their successful integration into the host embryo and for the production of F0 ES mouse pups.
